## Can AI conduct research for us?

\studycard

\cardhead{AI-written papers are weaker in ideas than in execution}

AI models rated 912 AI-written economics papers and 41 published papers [@li2026]

Execution scored 3.8 vs.\ 4.4 out of 5, but fewer ideas reached top-journal level (23% vs.\ 73%)

\studycardend

\studycard

\cardhead{AI agents do the technical work alone, but their papers are rejected}

AI agents had six days to answer the question of an unpublished paper [@kirgis2026]

The paper's authors reviewed the result: the conclusions did not follow from the evidence

\studycardend

In both studies, AI handles the technical work better than the ideas and the research judgment.

## How can skill-first help us do reproducible research?

\vspace{0.6em}

\begin{center}
\textbf{\textcolor{whu_blue}{Skill-first}} allows us to fix the process in a workflow, for us and for our AI agents.
\end{center}

```{=latex}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[
  card/.style={rounded corners=6pt,fill=whu_lightblue!10},
  num/.style={circle,fill=whu_blue,text=white,font=\large\bfseries,minimum size=0.8cm,inner sep=0pt},
  row/.style={anchor=north west,align=left,text width=11.9cm,inner sep=0pt,font=\normalsize,text=whu_anthracite}
]
  % each card follows the height of its text
  % benefit 1
  \node[row] (t1) at (-5.45,0) {{\large\bfseries\color{whu_blue} Clear goals and repeatable processes}\\[1pt]
    It forces us to set well-defined goals and processes, which is what reproducible research requires.};

  % benefit 2
  \node[row] (t2) at ($(t1.south west)+(0,-0.76)$) {{\large\bfseries\color{whu_blue} Clear roles for humans and agents}\\[1pt]
    It makes us decide where human judgment is needed and where steps can be delegated to (sub)agents when they don't need verification and can be forgotten.};

  \begin{scope}[on background layer]
    \fill[card] ($(t1.north west)+(-1.5,0.18)$) rectangle ($(t1.south east)+(0.5,-0.18)$);
    \fill[card] ($(t2.north west)+(-1.5,0.18)$) rectangle ($(t2.south east)+(0.5,-0.18)$);
  \end{scope}
  \node[num] at ($(t1.west)+(-0.75,0)$) {1};
  \node[num] at ($(t2.west)+(-0.75,0)$) {2};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}
```

## My current skill template

\vspace{0.6em}

\fitimage[\linewidth]{images/skill_workflow.pdf}

\begin{center}
See the \href{https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices}{\textcolor{whu_lightblue}{Anthropic documentation}} and \href{https://agentskills.io}{\textcolor{whu_lightblue}{agentskills.io}}.
\end{center}

## Example: the paper audit skill

**Purpose:** Does a full audit (mistakes, errors, inconsistencies, and fact-check) in a paper before it goes to a journal. The skill evaluates and reports. I decide what to fix.

1. I give it the paper, the appendix, the response letter, and the analysis output
2. It lists every table, figure, number, and reference in these files
3. It writes a short plan of the errors most likely in this paper
4. Four agents each check one part: references, tables, text, and the response letter
5. A fresh agent checks each finding against the paper and sets aside what it cannot confirm
6. Parts that were missed are checked again, for at most three rounds
7. I receive a report that ranks each mistake and gives its page and an exact quote

## The agent's role in the pipeline

- Agents follow the same rules as human researchers
- Delete all processed data and output: the code rebuilds everything
- **Role 1: agents edit the code, or help us edit it**
    - Already challenging, because AI makes mistakes
    - The researcher stays in the loop
- **Role 2: AI as a source of data**
    - Data an LLM touches becomes generated data, stored as raw data
    - AI never restructures, merges, or formats existing data: that is code's job

## AGENTS.md: rules for every agent

```text
# AGENTS.md (excerpt, shortened)
- Never modify the raw data in 0_data/.
- Never edit 2_process/ or 3_output/ by hand.
- Change only 1_code/, 4_drafts/, and the codebook.
- Before a multi-file change, say which files will change.
- Never run git commit or git push.
- Done only when "make clean" then "make" rebuilds everything.
```

- Git enables us to check and audit the changes made by AI agents (researcher-in-the-loop)

\source{\href{https://github.com/victorvanpelt/research_pipeline_example}{github.com/victorvanpelt/research\_pipeline\_example}}
